Maladaptive Strategies.value: control eating strictly to feel in control
I imagine getting revenge on the people responsible
go along with whatever others want to feel safe

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
Even when others tell me I am safe I find it impossible to believe it
Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger

Memory.value: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.
When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel isolated and set apart from others
I feel permanently humiliated by what happened
Somebody else would not have gotten into this situation

vignette: Sohan, a 41-year-old South Asian man and park ranger in his local state park, has been struggling with symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) for several months following a traumatic captivity experience. The event that triggered these symptoms occurred about six months ago when he was captured by a militant group during an unauthorized visit to a nearby national park. Sohan vividly remembers the moments leading up to his capture: walking alone in the dense forest, the sudden appearance of armed individuals, and their harsh treatment towards him. He recalls those traumatic events as discrete snapshots that occasionally flash into his mind, accompanied by physical pain in his body as if it were reliving the same experience again. Sometimes, he can recall these moments but feels completely numb, as though they happened to someone else. The trauma has left Sohan feeling isolated and set apart from others, a sentiment compounded by feelings of permanent humiliation stemming from his captivity. He often wonders how someone in similar circumstances might have avoided such a situation, leading him to feel deeply self-critical about the events that transpired. Sohan's triggers are closely tied to his experience: military topics, being seen by others, and authority figures dressed in uniform all evoke strong reactions from him. Recently, while attending a memorial event for fallen soldiers at the park, he found himself becoming extremely anxious as people discussed their experiences with the military. His anxiety only worsened when a group of veterans in uniform approached him to shake hands. He was startled by their movements and felt his heart racing, fearing that they might be part of the militant group. To cope with these intense feelings, Sohan has resorted to several maladaptive strategies. He strictly controls his eating habits as a way to feel more in control of his life, often skipping meals or consuming very small portions. His thoughts are frequently consumed by fantasies of getting revenge on those who were responsible for his captivity. Additionally, he often goes along with whatever others want him to do to maintain a sense of safety and avoid conflict. In the park, Sohan's avoidance behaviors have affected his relationships with coworkers and supervisors. He has started avoiding patrols that would require him to work near areas where uniformed personnel are present, leading to tension with his team and supervisors who have noticed his decreased participation in certain activities. His avoidance has also limited opportunities for personal growth within the park service. What finally brought Sohan to seek help was a particularly intense flashback while on patrol alone, which left him physically shaken and emotionally drained. He realized that he could no longer manage these overwhelming feelings on his own and feared that his symptoms would only worsen over time. Seeking help, he hopes for relief from the constant anxiety and intrusive memories, as well as to rebuild some sense of trust in others. Sohan is most afraid of never feeling safe again and being trapped by his painful memories. He hopes therapy can provide him with tools to regain control and reconnect with the world around him, without constantly feeling isolated or haunted by his past experiences.
